title: Make each wagon's capability boundary legible from its description

facts.note: Any planning, authoring or review task that touches or inspects a wagon; applies to every wagon, whether new, changed or unchanged.

values: wagon description does not convey what the wagon does and does not own
facts.note: Legibility of the capability boundary from the description alone can only be judged by a reader.

values: rationale-like field added to wagon schema or wagon entries
facts.note: Schema/diff observer needed to detect a new field carrying rationale instead of the existing description field.

fires: The planner adds a new wagon to the plan.
The planner edits a wagon's scope or description.
The planner or a reviewer inspects an existing, unchanged wagon whose description does not make clear what it does and does not own.
doesNotFire: Plan or doc content that does not define or describe any wagon.
Code changes unrelated to wagon definitions.

given: Any wagon in the plan, whether newly added, changed, or existing and unchanged
when: the planner writes, updates, or reviews that wagon's description
then: The description alone must make the wagon's capability boundary (what it does and does not own) understandable later without the original conversation.
prefer: Write the description so a later reader can understand, from it alone, what the wagon does and does not own.
Put the rationale in the existing wagon schema description field.
avoid: Introducing a new schema field (e.g. a separate rationale field) to carry the boundary or rationale.
Descriptions that only make sense with the planning conversation in hand (references to 'as discussed', unstated context).
why: Wagons outlive the conversation that created them, so a later reader must be able to tell from the description alone what the wagon owns and does not own. Reusing the existing description field keeps the schema unchanged.
evidence: Each wagon's description field, read in isolation, makes clear what the wagon does and does not own.
No new field was added to the wagon schema to hold rationale.
verifier_detail: Term capability_boundary: what the wagon does and does not own, legible from its description alone.
Term no_new_field: rationale rides the existing description field, not a new schema field.

additions.text: Descriptions that only make sense with the planning conversation in hand (references to 'as discussed', unstated context).
additions.justification: Concrete anti-pattern restating the source's 'without the original conversation' requirement; no new obligation.
Activation is required by the schema; it covers every wagon description (new, changed or unchanged), matching the source's 'each wagon' scope.
